key_insight: Fracture toughness of triangular and hexagonal lattices is governed by a transition from density-dependent beam-level fracture at low relative density to nodal stress-concentration-driven failure at high relative density, enabling an analytical model across both regimes.
engineering_relevance: Designers can tune lattice toughness by adjusting relative density, crack orientation, and nodal fillet radius, with quasi-brittle base materials offering additional toughness gains through localized plasticity.
method: Blunt-crack fracture theory for low-to-high relative density lattices
Finite element simulations plus PMMA fracture experiments
evidence_signal: Finite element results, analytical predictions, and laser-cut PMMA experiments jointly show good agreement and reveal a ~1.6× toughness increase for quasi-brittle lattices, with some cases exceeding base-material toughness.
watch_item: Brittle lattice fracture remains stochastic, especially at higher relative densities, so local geometry and crack-path variability must be considered in design and testing.
paper_title: Fracture of Lattice Materials from Low to High Relative Density
